booth-white.purpose: The page ground; the surround all colour judgement happens against.

booth-panel.purpose: Raised-by-tone surfaces: export code block, envelope plot grounds.

recessed-grey.purpose: Hover ground for bordered controls sitting on a panel.

hairline.purpose: The default 1px rule. Divides everything, asserts nothing.

scored-line.purpose: The emphatic rule: touchable controls, slider tracks, plot axes.

graphite-ink.purpose: Body and heading text, plot strokes, focus outline.

pencil-grey.purpose: Secondary prose, control hints, supporting table cells.

faint-pencil.purpose: The quietest ink: hue angles, axis labels, "none" placeholders. Still clears 4.5:1.

inverted-ground.purpose: The active/selected state. Stands in for a brand accent.

verified-green.purpose: A measured contrast pass. Never the sole signal.

flagged-red.purpose: A measured failure, and the border of an invalid colour field.

cautioned-amber.purpose: A guarantee that slipped below the contrast its position implies.

display.purpose: The inspector hex readout — the largest type in the product, and a figure. Underlined because it also copies.

headline.purpose: A colour family's name in the palette board.

title.purpose: Panel headings. The page h1 is a 14.5px semibold title, not a banner.

body.purpose: Explanatory prose and table cells. Measures capped 58–76ch.

label.purpose: Control group headings, buttons, menu items.

micro.purpose: Hints, badges, hue angles, seed notes. Down to 10px for swatch labels, 8px for SVG axes.

figure.purpose: Every number, hex, ratio and angle. Mono with tabular numerals, always.

shadows.name: floating-layer
shadows.purpose: Popovers and dropdown menus only — the two genuinely detached layers. Always paired with a Scored Line border so the layer keeps an edge in dark mode.

motion.name: swatch-lift
motion.purpose: The only transform in the product: a swatch raises on hover and lifts its z-index so it can be compared against its neighbours.

motion.name: border-shift
motion.purpose: A secondary button strengthening its border from Hairline to Graphite Ink on hover.

motion.name: reduced-motion-clamp
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every duration collapses. No design may depend on motion.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The workhorse control: Copy link, Copy, Save file. Square, hairline-bordered, never filled at rest; the border strengthens to full ink on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--app-ink); background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--app-line); border-radius: 0; padding: 4px 10px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 150ms, background 150ms; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: var(--app-ink); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--app-ink); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Primary Button (derived tint)
components.description: The one tinted element in the product. Filled with a shade derived from the colour the user entered, via the palette's computed value for that seed; the label uses that swatch's onHexWcag so it passes the standard the tool reports against. The inline custom properties stand in for the runtime values.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; width: 100%; height: 36px; padding: 0 10px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; background: var(--cta-bg); color: var(--cta-ink); border: 1px solid var(--app-line-strong); border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary-family { margin-left: auto; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--app-ink); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: A single hairline-bordered row divided by internal borders, never gaps. The selected segment inverts rather than tinting — the system's signature state gesture.
components.css: .ds-segmented { display: flex; border: 1px solid var(--app-line); } .ds-segment { flex: 1; padding: 4px 6px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--app-ink-muted); background: transparent; border: 0; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; } .ds-segment + .ds-segment { border-left: 1px solid var(--app-line); } .ds-segment:hover { color: var(--app-ink); } .ds-segment-selected, .ds-segment-selected:hover { background: var(--app-inverse-bg); color: var(--app-inverse-ink); } .ds-segment:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--app-ink); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Tabs
components.description: Panel switcher. The active tab carries a 2px ink bottom border; inactive tabs carry a transparent one of the same width so nothing shifts on change.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--app-line); } .ds-tab { padding: 6px 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; color: var(--app-ink-muted); background: transparent; border: 0; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--app-ink); } .ds-tab-active { color: var(--app-ink); font-weight: 500; border-bottom-color: var(--app-ink); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--app-ink); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Hex Input
components.description: Mono, tabular, 6.5rem wide. An unparseable value turns the border Flagged Red live and sets aria-invalid; blur reverts to the committed colour rather than leaving it broken.
components.html: <input class="ds-input-hex" value="#635bff" spellcheck="false" aria-label="Colour 1 value"><input class="ds-input-hex ds-input-hex-invalid" value="#zzz" spellcheck="false" aria-invalid="true" aria-label="Colour 2 value">
components.css: .ds-input-hex { width: 6.5rem; padding: 2px 6px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 12px; color: var(--app-ink); background: var(--app-bg); border: 1px solid var(--app-line); border-radius: 0; } .ds-input-hex + .ds-input-hex { margin-left: 8px; } .ds-input-hex-invalid { border-color: var(--app-fail); } .ds-input-hex:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--app-ink); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Instrument Slider
components.description: A range input restyled to read as calibrated hardware rather than an OS widget: a 2px Scored Line track and a 4px x 16px ink blade. Its value prints as a mono figure beside the group heading.
components.html:
Families10

Colours spread around the wheel from yours.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; min-width: 8.5rem; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field-head { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; } .ds-field-label { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--app-ink); } .ds-field-value { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--app-ink-muted); } .ds-hint { margin: 0; font-size: 11px; line-height: 1.35; color: var(--app-ink-muted); } .ds-slider { appearance: none; -webkit-appearance: none; width: 100%; height: 24px; background: transparent; cursor: ew-resize; } .ds-slider::-webkit-slider-runnable-track { height: 2px; background: var(--app-line-strong); } .ds-slider::-moz-range-track { height: 2px; background: var(--app-line-strong); } .ds-slider::-webkit-slider-thumb { appearance: none; -webkit-appearance: none; width: 4px; height: 16px; margin-top: -7px; background: var(--app-ink); border: 0; border-radius: 1px; } .ds-slider::-moz-range-thumb { width: 4px; height: 16px; background: var(--app-ink); border: 0; border-radius: 1px; } .ds-slider:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--app-ink); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Swatch Ramp
components.description: The signature component. Swatches sit in a grid with a 1px gutter so a ramp reads as one continuous band. Each labels itself in its own onHexWcag; a seed carries a 2px inset ring in that same colour, drawn as a real span overlay so it never displaces the grid. Hover lifts to 1.04. Selection uses the same overlay technique with a 2px ink outline at 2px offset.
components.css: .ds-ramp { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 1px; } .ds-swatch { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; height: 80px; padding: 6px; text-align: left; border: 0; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; transition: transform 150ms; } .ds-swatch:hover { z-index: 10; transform: scale(1.04); } .ds-swatch:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--app-ink); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-swatch-label { font-size: 10px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; } .ds-swatch-hex { font-size: 9.5px; line-height: 1; } .ds-swatch-ring { position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; left: 0; border: 2px solid currentColor; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Pass and fail marks. Colour is the redundant channel: every badge is an icon and a word, so the meaning survives greyscale and colour-vision deficiency.
components.html: AAFail600 below usual contrast
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; margin-right: 12px; white-space: nowrap; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; } .ds-badge-pass { color: var(--app-pass); } .ds-badge-fail { color: var(--app-fail); } .ds-badge-warn { color: var(--app-warn); }

components.name: Yours Badge
components.description: Marks a family that came from a colour the user supplied. An outline, not a fill — it labels without adding colour to the surround.
components.css: .ds-badge-yours { display: inline-block; padding: 1px 4px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; color: var(--app-ink); border: 1px solid var(--app-ink); border-radius: 0; }

components.name: Code Block
components.description: The export preview. Focusable so keyboard users can scroll it, labelled by format, on a Booth Panel ground with a hairline border.
components.css: .ds-code { max-height: 26rem; margin: 0; overflow: auto; padding: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 11.5px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--app-ink); background: var(--app-surface); border: 1px solid var(--app-line); border-radius: 0; } .ds-code:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--app-ink); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
Colour professionals do not judge a sample in a decorated room. They judge it in a viewing booth: a standardised, deliberately colourless enclosure whose walls are grey precisely so that nothing in the room contributes an opinion about the sample. This interface is that booth. Every surface, rule, label and control is achromatic, and the only colour on screen is the palette the user is there to evaluate. This is not a stylistic preference that could be traded for a warmer look — a tinted interface biases the judgement the tool exists to support, so the achromatic shell is load-bearing.

The character is quiet, deferential and exact. The interface's job is to disappear. Restraint is the entire personality: nothing competes with the palette, nothing is decorative, and no element asks for attention it has not earned. Where a lesser system would reach for an accent colour, a fill, a gradient or a shadow, this one reaches for a hairline rule, a change of weight, or inversion. Depth comes from three rule weights and two surface tones, not from light. Corners are square everywhere — the only radii in the system are a 2px focus ring and a 1px slider thumb, both functional.

Density is professional and unapologetic in service of one rule: everything that shapes the result sits above the palette, in a single band, so nothing is hidden below the fold or off to one side. Type runs from 17px down to 8px, with the working range between 11px and 12.5px. Every figure is set in mono with tabular numerals, because figures in this tool exist to be compared in columns. The largest type on the screen is not a headline — it is a hex code.
keyCharacteristics: Achromatic shell; the generated palette is the only colour, with one derived exception
Zero corner radius; hairline rules and inversion carry all structure
Flat at rest — no shadow on any resting element
Mono, tabular figures throughout; the display role is a figure
Every input in one band above the palette
Pass and fail never carried by colour alone: always an icon and a word
Light and dark are peers, both defined token-for-token

rules.name: The Viewing Booth Rule
rules.body: The chrome is achromatic. No accent hue, no tinted surface, no coloured border, no coloured focus ring. Focus, selection and active states are carried by weight, rule and inversion. The palette is the only colour on screen.

rules.name: The Derived Tint Rule
rules.body: Chrome may take colour from the generated palette when it is the primary action, and it must derive that colour from what the user entered — resolved through the palette's own computed value for that seed, never the raw input and never a hardcoded hue. Two conditions hold whenever it does: the label is drawn in the swatch's onHexWcag so the element passes the standard the tool reports against, and the tinted element never becomes the surround for a swatch being judged.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: No pass, fail or warning is communicated by colour alone. Every status mark carries an icon and a word.

rules.name: The Faint Still Reads Rule
rules.body: Faint Pencil labels 8-11px hue angles and axis values, which WCAG treats as body text, so it must clear 4.5:1 against its ground. Quietness stops at the threshold, not past it.

rules.name: The Mono Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number is set in mono with tabular numerals. Figures in this tool exist to be compared down a column, and proportional digits break that.

rules.name: The No Display Type Rule
rules.body: There is no hero type and no room for it. The scale tops out at 17px, and that slot belongs to a measured value.

rules.name: The Everything Above Rule
rules.body: Every input that shapes the result lives in one band above the palette. The colours come first and take the most room; everything else is an adjustment to what those colours already produced.

rules.name: The Hairline Gutter Rule
rules.body: Swatches within a ramp are separated by exactly 1px of page ground, never by margin, radius or shadow. The ramp is one object.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow is permitted only on an element that is genuinely floating above the page and will disappear again. If it is still there after the next click, it has no shadow.

rules.name: The Rules Are The Depth Rule
rules.body: Reach for a rule weight before a surface tone, and a surface tone before a shadow. Hairline divides, Scored Line invites touch, inversion means active.

rules.name: The Zero Radius Rule
rules.body: New components have square corners. If a rounded corner seems needed, the real problem is that the element is competing for attention it should not have.

rules.name: The Two Rule Weights Rule
rules.body: A border is Hairline or Scored Line, and the difference is meaning, not decoration: Scored Line says "you can act on this".

dos: Do keep the chrome achromatic. Use the Neutral scale, inversion, and rule weight to build every state.

Do derive any tinted chrome from the user's entered colour through the palette's computed value for it, label it with that swatch's onHexWcag, and keep it out of the surround of anything being judged.
Do set every number in mono with tabular numerals via .tabular.
Do use square corners (border-radius: 0) on new components.
Do pick a border weight semantically: Hairline to divide, Scored Line to invite action.
Do put new inputs that shape the output into the top control band, with a 12px medium heading, a mono value readout, and an 11px hint.
Do pair every status colour with an icon and a word.
Do give every control an aria-label, and sliders an aria-valuetext in plain language.
Do define light and dark values together for any new token. Both themes are first-class.
Do preview continuously and commit once on release for any dragged control, so one gesture is one history entry.
donts: Don't introduce an accent hue, a coloured focus ring, a coloured border or a tinted surface into the chrome.
Don't put a shadow on anything that stays on the page. Shadow is for floating layers only, and they get a Scored Line border too.
Don't round a corner. The only radii are the 2px focus ring and the 1px slider thumb.
Don't introduce display type. The scale stops at 17px, and that slot is a measured value.
Don't use proportional digits for a quantity.
Don't communicate pass, fail or warning by colour alone.
Don't move an output-shaping input below the palette, behind a disclosure, or into the sidebar.
Don't let Faint Pencil drop below 4.5:1 against its ground, however small the text.
Don't use onHex for the tool's own labels — that is the perceptual recommendation for the user's output. The interface uses onHexWcag so it passes the standard it reports.
Don't animate anything beyond the swatch's 1.04 hover scale and simple colour transitions; prefers-reduced-motion clamps everything to 0.01ms and the design must not depend on motion.
